_comment: This is the ONLY file you should need to edit. 'paths' tells the suite where your binary lives; 'implemented' tells it which flags your grep supports so it only runs applicable cases. Everything else has a sensible default. judge_candidate.sh overrides both on a throwaway copy and never writes here.
_oracle_contract: suites/ was frozen against GNU grep 3.12, invoked as 'grep -a -F [-i] [-H|-h] -e PATTERN -- OPERAND' under LC_ALL=C -- a literal-substring matcher with no binary-file suppression and ASCII-only folding, which is new_grep's contract. oracle_version_required pins the release; gen/generate.py refuses to regenerate against another one, and refuses again if the binary fails the behavioral precheck in gen/oracle.py. Ten cases assert which options new_grep accepts or rejects and cannot come from any real grep; they stay model-derived and are listed by name in suites/MANIFEST.json. Re-pin only when deliberately re-freezing the benchmark.

paths._comment: oracle_bin: a GNU grep binary, used only to regenerate suites/ -- NOT needed to judge a candidate against the committed suites/. Prefer the GREP_ORACLE_BIN environment variable over editing this file, so a checkout does not carry one machine's layout: GREP_ORACLE_BIN=/usr/bin/grep. On Linux/WSL /usr/bin/grep is already GNU. On macOS the system /usr/bin/grep is BSD, not GNU -- install GNU grep (brew install grep) and point at its gnubin grep or at ggrep. The Git-for-Windows grep is GNU but is built in text mode and fails the precheck.
paths._comment1b: candidate_bin: your normal (non-instrumented) build. Required for runner.py. For example: agentic_cyber/build/new_grep
paths._comment2: candidate_asan_bin: an ASan/UBSan-instrumented build. Optional; runner.py --sanitizer uses it. Leave candidate_src empty to bring your own instead of having build_asan.sh compile one.
paths._comment3: candidate_src / cc / cc_flags: only used by build_asan.sh, only if your grep is a single C source file you want this suite to compile with sanitizers.

_comment4: The oracle is needed only to REGENERATE suites/. Judging a candidate compares against the committed goldens byte for byte and runs no grep at all, so no oracle ships with these tests and none is ever copied into a sandbox (scripts/stage_test_bundle.py rebuilds this file from an allowlist that excludes paths.oracle_bin).
_comment5: implemented: flag IDs your binary currently supports. A frozen case only runs if every ID in its own 'flags' list appears here. The list below is a placeholder -- the experiment harness supplies the cumulative checkpoint list at runtime.
